newsitem.title: ISRAEL: FBI chief, Israel minister discuss Hamas leader.
newsitem.headline: FBI chief, Israel minister discuss Hamas leader.

text.p: FBI Director Louis Freeh and Israeli Justice Minister Tsahi Hanegbi have discussed a leader of the Islamic group Hamas who is awaiting extradition from the United States, Israel's justice ministry said on Tuesday.

Israeli security sources have said Israeli, Jordanian and U.S. officials are secretly examining a deal to send the Hamas leader, Mousa Abu Marzook, to Amman in return for his promise to shun violence.

"It was a get-to-know-you meeting between the minister and the FBI head. He (Abu Marzook) was mentioned in passing, not in a working sense," a spokeswoman for Israel's Justice Ministry told Reuters of Monday's meeting.
Israel has alleged that Abu Marzook, as political leader of the militant Hamas, was responsible for Hamas attacks that killed scores of Israelis. It demanded his extradition.

Abu Marzook has said he was involved only in political matters for which he could not be extradited. But last month, after 18 months in a New York jail, he dropped his court challenge to Israel's demand that U.S. officials hand him over.

Hamas has warned of guerrilla attacks should Abu Marzook be extradited to Israel. Palestinian President Yasser Arafat -- whose peace deals with Israel have been violently opposed by Hamas -- asked the United States not to send him to Israel.

Jordanian Justice Minister Abdul Karim al-Dughmi said on Friday that Jordan's King Hussein was working for the release on humanitarian grounds of Abu Marzook and of Hamas founder Sheikh Ahmed Yassin, who is held by Israel.
